universe.name: Studio Lumina
universe.why: A QR code is literally a grid of binary data. Making it a physical, interactive glowing floor turns abstract algebra into a tangible puzzle that visually rebuilds itself.
universe.pacing: Deliberate and mechanical, escalating into frantic slapstick, ending in an abrupt deadpan stop.
universe.signature_shot: The penguin standing in pitch darkness with only its glowing white eye-rings visible after shattering the crucial corner square.
universe.medium_break: The penguin destroys the corner tile and the entire medium's lighting grid hard-cuts to black, shutting down the universe.
universe.look_bible: Retro-futuristic 1980s arcade light-floor medium. Thick frosted glass tiles (pure white and obsidian black) set in a heavy brushed steel grid. Illuminated from beneath with intense neon glows. Deep shadows, volumetric fog rolling across the floor, anamorphic lens flares, macro scale depth of field. Palette: obsidian, frosted white, neon magenta, cyan. The motion feels like heavy physical switches clicking and glass sliding.
universe.penguin_render: Chubby steel/acrylic penguin with a brushed steel back, frosted white acrylic belly, glowing neon orange feet, and three thin steel wire feathers on top.
universe.music: 1980s synthwave arcade loop with heavy bass pulses and analog synthesizer arpeggios, instrumental

penguin.arc: Wants to destroy the floor for fun, gets frustrated when it keeps repairing itself, finally discovers the fatal flaw and ruins it completely.
